title: Elastic Headroom Manager and Overage Attenuation Policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers running Dedicated capacity sometimes encounter short-lived demand spikes. Our current model gives them an automatic temporary boost from a global surge pool and then bills at overage rates. This has led to unpredictability in invoices and support tickets asking for bill adjustments. Goal: Implement an "Elastic Headroom Manager" (EHM) to control short-duration boosts, document a deterministic attenuation policy for overage billing, and provide operational controls to both product teams and customers to minimize surprise charges while preserving platform availability.
background_and_context: We already support surge pools and reserve lanes but have inconsistent attenuation and reconciliation behavior across regions.
Recent false-positive spikes caused 3 high-severity support incidents in Q4 2024; customers reported unexpected overage invoices.
Existing tickets reference: ENG-28716 (preemptible reserve lanes) and ENG-24680 (reserve lanes credit expiry). Those provide partial building blocks but not a coherent attenuation manager.
Primary trade-offs are availability during spikes vs predictable customer billing and operator overhead for manual reconciliations.
goals: 1) Implement EHM that rates and buckets short-lived bursts using a configurable time-decay headroom token model.

2) Ensure deterministic invoice attenuation rules: when a short boost is granted and usage drops back within X minutes, automatically flag for pro-rata billing adjustment rather than full overage billing.
3) Expose per-customer policy controls (aggressive / balanced / conservative) with sensible defaults and a visible expected-cost delta in Console.
4) Add observability: per-boost audit logs, burn-rate dashboards, and automated customer notifications when attenuation applies.
acceptance_criteria: EHM accepts configuration per-customer and per-pool and enforces boost durations and credit decay as defined in design doc.

Attenuation policy implemented so that boosts lasting < 10 minutes with subsequent sustained usage drop are billed with a 50% pro-rata attenuated overage for the affected window (configurable by tier).
Console shows a clear indicator on Dedicated capacity pages when a boost is in effect and an estimated incremental cost delta in USD for the current hour.
Automated tests covering headroom token refills, borrow, and rollback; unit and integration tests for billing adjustments.
E2E performance tests show <3% P50 latency increase when serving from surge pool vs baseline pool under typical loads.
design_summary: Headroom model: per-customer token bucket with time-based decay. Tokens represent GPU-second headroom. Normal refill rate equals customer's reserved throughput; tokens can be borrowed up to a configurable cap.
Boost lifecycle: grant, monitor, classify as transient or persistent (transient if returned to baseline within T minutes), then if transient mark for attenuation pipeline.

Attenuation pipeline: flagged windows are summarized and sent to billing reconciler which applies pro-rata credit rather than full overage charge. A retention of reason codes and audit trail stored in billing logs.
Operational controls: global operator override, per-customer policy toggles, and a bounded reconciliation queue to prevent unbounded manual work.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Risk: overly lenient attenuation could be gamed by customers to avoid paying for legitimate sustained bursts. Mitigation: require sustained drop for at least T_min minutes and limit attenuation frequency per billing cycle.
Risk: complexity in billing pipeline increases reconciliation surface. Mitigation: keep attenuation rules declarative and limited to a small number of predicates to simplify audits.
Availability vs cost: Conservative policies reduce surprise billing but may throttle user experiences during spikes. Expose policy modes so customers choose their preference.
Operational risk: additional state needs to be replicated in control plane; plan to shard by customer and cap memory retention windows.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Proto EHM service (read-only simulation) + shipping design doc to infra and billing teams.
Phase 2 (3 weeks): Implement grant/monitor/classify flows, in-memory token buckets, metrics, and console indicators. Deploy to staging.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Implement attenuation pipeline in billing reconciler with test invoice generation and dry-run mode.
Phase 4 (2 weeks): Canary to 5% of customers on Dedicated, monitor key metrics, run billing dry-run and manual verification.
Phase 5 (1 week): Rollout to GA with customer communication and support playbook.
